excluded_inline_probes.role: INTERPRETER CAPABILITY PROBE, added round 6. It asks whether the ACTIVE python3 can run the preflight tools at all, and prints the answer in the failure branch. It invokes the interpreter itself, never a repository module, so mnv_guarded_run.py has nothing to contain -- routing it through the guard would assert that an interpreter resolves its own imports inside the code root, which is meaningless.
excluded_inline_probes.why_it_exists: Round 5 shipped one launcher whose Python preflight tools ran BEFORE the activator; on the un-activated 3.6.15 interpreter they die with a SyntaxError and the launcher reported 'the execution tree is not the tree that was approved' -- a wrong diagnosis of a right refusal.

OI-179 defect 3: asserts every MNV_* the submission baseline declares reached this task, and records the task's own environment. Excluded on the same ground as the two above, which is CIRCULARITY, not stdlib-purity -- see `exclusion_criterion` (5) and `exclusion_criterion_5_was_corrected_by_measurement`. Measured repo_origin_count=0, so mnv_guarded_run.py has nothing to contain. Its executing copy IS bound, by an A-3 --pair entry in every declared launcher, which is the protection that actually applies to a preflight tool.

exclusion_criterion: A python3 invocation may be declared a preflight exclusion only if ALL FIVE hold, each machine-checked. (1) the entry names `shell_var`, `resolves_to` and `role`, all non-empty. (2) `<VAR>="${CODE_ROOT}/<resolves_to>"` appears in EVERY declared launcher. (3) it is invoked exactly `per_launcher` times in EVERY declared launcher. (4) its executing copy is A-3 `--pair` bound in EVERY declared launcher -- this is the protection that actually applies to a preflight tool, and it was verified by hand for OI-185 and is now enforced. (5) THE GUARD HAS NOTHING TO CONTAIN BUT ITSELF: running `mnv_guarded_run.py` over the tool yields `repo_origins` that are a SUBSET OF {mnv_guarded_run}. (1)-(4) are byte-level and enforced by mnv_preflight_census.py. (5) requires EXECUTING the tool, so it lives in test_k0_preflight_exclusion_census.py::test_the_exclusion_criterion_is_MEASURED_not_asserted, with a power arm that fires on a tool importing anything else. UNDER THIS, A PRINCIPLED PREFLIGHT TOOL NEEDS NO RULING AND AN UNPRINCIPLED ONE STILL FAILS, which answers F-7(a) structurally instead of numerically.
exclusion_criterion_5_was_corrected_by_m: RESOLVED 2026-09-01 -- JOSEPH, SHOWN THE DEPARTURE BELOW: 'I don't think I meant it literally.' The criterion in `exclusion_criterion` (5) is the binding one. WHAT WAS DISCLOSED TO HIM, KEPT UNCHANGED BECAUSE IT IS WHAT HE WAS SHOWN: criterion (5) as proposed in OI-185 was WRONG, and the measurement corrected it rather than the rule being relaxed to fit. The row, and the recommendation he ratified, gave the ground as 'imports only the standard library'. Measured 2026-09-01 with `mnv_guarded_run.py --expect-root <repo> --inventory`: mnv_env_provenance.py checked=13 repo_origin_count=0; pet/verify_executing_copy_is_committed.py checked=14 repo_origin_count=0; BUT mnv_source_manifest.py checked=15 repo_origin_count=1 -- it imports `MARKERS, is_checkout` from mnv_guarded_run itself at mnv_source_manifest.py:61. A stdlib-only rule would therefore have FIRED ON AN ENTRY RULING 21 ALREADY ACCEPTED, i.e. on every correct tree. The correct scope came from restating the question, not from loosening it: the ground already written in `why_these_are_excluded` is CIRCULARITY -- routing these through the guard would make the check depend on the thing it is checking -- and 'no repository import except the guard itself' is exactly that ground made falsifiable. All three entries satisfy it as measured.
ratification: Joseph, 2026-09-01, OI-185: 'Okay I like your recommendation for OI-185, do it.' RECORDED IN docs/orchestration/DECISION-20260901-joseph-ratifies-oi185-invariants.md, which reproduces VERBATIM the recommendation that ruling accepts and the pre-ruling flag that the structural half needed his say-so. THAT FILE GOVERNS; this field is a pointer. SECTION 4 IS RESOLVED: the shipped criterion is broader than the ratified words by exactly one module, on measurement; that departure was disclosed to Joseph before he blessed it and he ruled 2026-09-01 'I don't think I meant it literally'. The stdlib-only phrasing was descriptive of the tool that prompted the row, not a criterion he was fixing. No code, test or declaration changed as a result -- only the authorization stopped being provisional. TWO things were ratified and both are implemented here. (1) THE BOUNDARY STANDS AT 14 GUARDED / 38 GUARDING-BOUNDARY. Ruling 21's subject is the GUARDED count, which did not move; OI-179 defect-3 enforcement is a legitimate preflight exclusion on the criterion in `exclusion_criterion`. (2) THE AUTHORED TOTALS ARE REPLACED BY INVARIANTS, which is a change to how ruling 21 is ENFORCED and is why it needed his say-so. Before this, `excluded_preflight` (24), `non_comment_python3_invocations` (54), `inline_interpreter_probes` (16) and `launchers` (8) were numbers a human wrote down. Each moved every time a preflight tool was added, each move cost a ruling, and none of them protected anything the per-launcher per-tool checks did not already cover. THEY ARE GONE FROM THIS FILE -- not bumped, not relaxed. The census DERIVES them from this file's own per-launcher structure and PRINTS them. A number that is recorded but not enforced is the defect OI-179 named ('a value computed, printed into records, and asserted only for STABILITY is a datum nobody has shown can disagree'), so the totals are not written down here at all -- cite the census's output, which is derived at read time.
what_the_three_pins_are_for: guarded=14 is RULING 21's PIN and the only count here that still requires a ruling to move: it is the set of science invocations routed through mnv_guarded_run.py. unclassified=0 is the F-7(a) invariant -- an invocation that is neither guarded nor declared is a violation, and zero is not a magic number. commented_out_python3_lines=18 is a TRIPWIRE, not part of the boundary: commenting out a guarded call removes a guard while leaving the line visible, so the count is pinned to make that a finding. It is kept pinned deliberately -- OI-185 ratified de-pinning the BOUNDARY TOTALS, and quietly de-pinning an unrelated tripwire on the way past would be exactly the scope creep this campaign files against.
what_this_pins: The set of python3 invocations in the declared k=0 launchers that are DELIBERATELY not routed through mnv_guarded_run.py, and the INVARIANTS that make the exclusion falsifiable. Before this file the exclusion was implicit: nothing named the sixteen, and nothing failed if a seventeenth appeared (Gate-1 F-7(a)). Since OI-185 it pins invariants rather than totals -- see `exclusion_criterion`.
why_that_last_number_is_here: About commented_out_python3_lines. A census that does not exclude comments reports a larger figure, and commenting out a guarded call is a way to REMOVE a guard while leaving the line visible. The number is pinned so that a change in it is a finding rather than a rounding difference between two instruments.
why_these_are_excluded: They ARE the preflight. mnv_guarded_run.py checks that imports resolve inside --expect-root; the two preflight tools are what establish that the executing copy IS the declared root. Routing them through the guard would make the check depend on the thing it is checking. They are excluded from the GUARD; they are NOT excluded from binding -- both are --pair'd and both are covered by the source manifest, asserted separately.
